subject: deployment-contract
seam_note: The chart defends the single-writer invariant three ways INSIDE the pod spec (replicas: 1, Recreate, ReadWriteOnce) and was undefended against the two things a platform does to a pod from outside: a node drain, and a credential that changes in the Secret object while the container keeps the value it read at start.
a: PodDisruptionBudget objects rendered: 0 — `kubectl drain` evicts the only replica and kp is down for a reschedule plus a PVC reattach, with nothing telling the administrator this workload is a single writer. Rendering the parent chart with auth.secret=y and with auth.secret=ROTATED produces a BYTE-IDENTICAL pod template (measured with diff), so `helm upgrade --set auth.secret=<new>` reports success while the container holds the old value.
b: 1 PodDisruptionBudget (minAvailable: 1, values-gated podDisruptionBudget.enabled, same selector as the Deployment) — voluntary eviction is refused with the budget named. The same rotation now changes checksum/secret (7f3d48f4… -> 72d32b1a…) so the pod rolls; policies 14 -> 16, each with a must-fail fixture.
instrument: helm template via alpine/helm in docker: kind census before/after, and the pod template diffed across two renders differing only in auth.secret, run against a `git archive` of the base chart and against this one; node scripts/deploy/__tests__/check-chart.test.mjs
gate: npm run deploy:check clean (16 policies); npm run test:deploy 23 -> 25 checks; node scripts/docs/check-doc-sync-diff.mjs --base 2780c901 --head HEAD clean; npm run docs:check clean; npx eslint clean
return_condition: minAvailable: 1 blocks ALL voluntary eviction. No doc in the tree names a managed cluster with unattended node rotation, where the strong form can stall a control-plane upgrade — if kp is ever deployed to one, the honest artifact is maxUnavailable: 1 (visible in the PDB status) plus a NOTES line, which is why the object is values-gated. And with existingSecret the chart renders no Secret to hash, so the checksum covers the values path only; self-hosting.md now tells that operator to roll the pod themselves.
note: The drain itself was not run (no cluster); the measured half is the rendered object and the rotation diff. Rotating KP_SECRET is a supported operation with named consequences in the app (bridge-client.ts refuses with "KP_SECRET … has changed since pairing"), so the falsifier that would have inverted this — a pod holding the old value is accidentally protective — does not fire: KP_SECRET also signs sessions (edge-verify.ts), and a pod that never re-reads it keeps honouring credentials the operator believes are retired.

The premise this run started from (the domains are declared and merely not sent) was refuted by the instrument: they are not declared either, so the registry technique's precondition needs the extra step, and the technique's 'derive the enumeration from the same declared bound the validation door reads' rule is what names it.
correction: This row FIRST said '17 domain repairs' and '13 tests', and kp's pre-push agent review refuted both across two rounds. Round 1: the instrument counted every max(0,min(...)) shape, so 6 clamps on locally computed values (a gate pass rate, a cosine, a time.sleep duration, two weighted sub-scores, a percentage formatter) inflated a gap no schema can close, and one mechanism was counted twice (a validator's decorator and the clamp in its own body) - real figure 10. Round 2: 10 is a FLOOR, not a count, because the patterns miss the scopeRung if/elif ladder at appmaster.py:672-682 and _clamp_prob at calibration_drift.py:65 - both of which this row itself cites as seam evidence. Floor is now 12 and says so. The same round caught the table being keyed by line number in a shared checkout, where one sibling's added import would have failed the gate on an unrelated commit; re-keyed by code marker. Round 3 caught three more: the work item still quoted the retracted 10 and a stale test count while the instrument printed 12 (a plan is what a later run executes from, not the ledger row, so it would have declared 10 domains, watched repairs_matched hit 0 and reported the gap closed with both hand-listed repairs still live); the regression guard asserted over hits of every kind, so the 6 local clamps the plan forbids touching would have kept it green forever; and the completeness assertions turned all of pipeline/jobfit into a tripwire - @field_validator is a routine addition here, so a sibling session adding one would red the Python gate pointing at a table in a file they never opened. The tripwire is removed: an unclassified hit now makes the instrument withhold every repair figure and print the offending sites instead - withheld rather than annotated, because a figure printed beside a warning gets quoted without the warning. That is where a sizing tool's signal belongs, and it is not somebody else's gate. Also replaced the boolean schema_enforced with constraint_sent in {none, mime, schema}: it read True for a mime-only call - claiming the model had been told field domains it was never told - and could not have survived step 3 sending a real schema, where True would mean two different things. Round 4 caught three consequences of round 3 and one older thing: the plan's step 3 still told a later run to reuse schema_enforced and forbade a second flag, which after the rename would have sent it grepping for an identifier that no longer exists - and it never said that step 3's actual job is to set the third state, constraint_sent = 'schema'. The ledger claimed figures were withheld when _render printed them above the warning; the code now does what this field said. And constraint_sent declared its closed set only in a comment, typed as a bare str - a value domain known, written in prose, and unreadable by the machines on either boundary, which is verbatim the defect this instrument exists to count. It is now ConstraintSent = Literal['none','mime','schema'] with the runtime tuple derived by get_args rather than retyped, and a test asserting every branch of the request builder emits a declared value.
